findings.line: bhaskar_agent.py:186-187; base_graph.py:3449 → 1737 (load_role); base.py:39-41 (raise); caught at bhaskar_agent.py:205-215
findings.finding: load_role() raises FileNotFoundError for a missing roles/<name>.md (base.py:39-41). build_agent_graph calls _make_call_llm_node unconditionally (base_graph.py:3449), which calls load_role(role_name) at node-construction time (base_graph.py:1737). There is no roles/bhaskar_agent.md (roles/ has 86 files, zero matching bhaskar). run_agent_graph raises before any LLM call; run_bhaskar_agent's own except catches it and returns ok=false. Every bhaskar_tool call fails, with zero tokens spent, on every path.
findings.evidence: Runtime-proved at HEAD c927c44b (fails before any API call): .venv/bin/python -c "from app.agents.bhaskar_agent import run_bhaskar_agent; print(run_bhaskar_agent('Write a script that prints hello','','/tmp'))" → {'ok': False, 'code': '', 'result_summary': '', 'tested_output': '', 'error': 'bhaskar_agent run failed: Role file not found: /home/pc-117/Documents/CRR2906/backend/roles/bhaskar_agent.md', 'tokens_in': 0, 'tokens_out': 0}. Feature default-enabled (config.py:1802-1805) and wired into chat_agent.py:115,4302-4312; tools.py:78-80,1348,1668-1674,1693; and ≥8 agent tool lists (bug_fix.py:55, mcp_developer_agent.py:69, migration_agent.py:51, user_story_generator.py:39, evaluation_agent.py:39, devex_agent.py:43, ux_design_agent.py:55, test_coverage_agent.py:46). Tests never exercise the real path — tests/test_bhaskar_tool.py:983-1026 monkeypatches run_agent_graph, so CI stays green.
findings.production_impact: The advertised on-demand tool synthesis capability never works: agents and chat users asking for a missing tool always get the structured failure. bhaskar_tool is non-functional while appearing wired, tested and enabled.
findings.recommendation: Add backend/roles/bhaskar_agent.md (7 standard sections + Karpathy variant), or extend the graph to accept an inline system prompt for this call. Add a regression test asserting load_role() succeeds for every role_name= literal passed to run_agent_graph anywhere in app/.

findings.finding: Submission payloads are schema-validated at the shared chokepoint but violations only log a warning and attach _validation_warning; the submission is still accepted. 0 of 27 submit tools use pydantic/BaseModel; handlers mostly dict.update(inp)/.get(). Mitigations exist: enforce_in_result overwrites model-claimed result fields with harness truth; file:line citations are verified against the repo; a quality gate runs; the sampled consumer qa.py:257-272 uses fail-closed defaults. But nothing known reads _validation_warning, so a schema-invalid submission is materially indistinguishable from a valid one at most call sites.
findings.evidence: ls app/tools/agents/submit_*.py | wc -l → 27; grep -l 'pydantic|BaseModel' app/tools/agents/submit_*.py → 0; base_graph.py:2883-2893 warning-only handling; qa.py:260-272 fail-closed raw.get(...) defaults; submit_qa_result.py:114-116 qa_result.update(inp).
findings.production_impact: Malformed-but-accepted submissions flow into result dicts; consumers that do not individually default fail-closed may act on bad data. The trust boundary is advisory, not enforced.
findings.confidence: High (behavior), Medium (downstream blast radius — one consumer sampled)
findings.recommendation: Decide explicitly: reject submissions that fail their declared input_schema (at least for high-risk/coder-class agents), or document the deliberate warn-only choice and make at least the quality gate read _validation_warning. Optionally adopt pydantic models per submit tool.

findings.line: 412-420 (_chat_agents dict, get_or_create_chat_agent), 437 (delete_chat_agent); no lock present (re-checked at HEAD c927c44b)
findings.finding: The session→agent map is module-level with a check-then-set and a pop, with no lock. Today all callers are async route handlers on the single event loop with no await between check and set, so it is serialized in practice. The per-instance _background_processes map (line 882) is confirmed per-instance (the known fix is intact).
findings.evidence: chat_agent.py:412-420, 437; callers only app/api/chat.py routes (chat.py:200,343,380,426); grep at HEAD c927c44b shows no lock around _chat_agents.
findings.production_impact: None today. If a caller later invokes these from a worker thread, concurrent get/create can leak two ChatAgents for one session, orphaning background processes the second instance cannot stop.
findings.recommendation: Add a small lock around get/create/pop, or document the event-loop-only invariant.
